name: Hul declared at Bhognadih
summary: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu told a gathering that Thakur Bonga had ordered the Santhal to end the rule of mahajan, zamindar, and Company in the Damin-i-Koh. The hul had a date.

reports.headline: A date in the Damin-i-Koh
reports.excerpt: The hul begins as a meeting. The muskets come later.

reports.headline: The Santal Hul: arrows against muskets
reports.excerpt: Peter Stanley’s reading of the hul: a meeting at Bhognadih, then muskets. The death band is still a range, not a register.

name: Meerut
summary: Sowars and sepoys of the Bengal Army rose on a Sunday, freed comrades from the jail, killed British officers and civilians, and rode for Delhi.

casualties.sideLabel: British officers and civilians in Meerut
casualties.note: Named European dead in Meerut are in the contemporary lists; Indian dead that night are not a single figure.

reports.headline: A Sunday in Meerut
reports.excerpt: The ride to Delhi is the political act. Meerut is the spark that had been drying for a season of cartridges, annexations, and rumours.

reports.headline: Meerut to Delhi
reports.excerpt: Sowars and sepoys rose on a Sunday, freed the jail, and rode for Delhi. The museum’s mutiny file still starts on 10 May.

name: Delhi taken
summary: The Meerut men entered Delhi. British officers on the Ridge and in the city were killed. Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed; he was old, and the sepoys needed a name.

casualties.sideLabel: British civilians and officers in Delhi, 11 May
casualties.note: Named European dead; Indian servants and bystanders are poorly counted.

reports.headline: A king because a city needed one
reports.excerpt: The proclamation in the Red Fort is not a plan. It is a fact the sepoys made, and the emperor survived as a symbol until the recapture.

reports.headline: A king because a city needed one
reports.excerpt: The Meerut men entered Delhi on 11 May. Bahadur Shah was proclaimed. The Ridge would spend the summer looking down on that fact.

name: Bibighar, Kanpur
summary: After the Sati Chaura ghat killings, surviving British women and children held at the Bibighar in Kanpur were killed on 15 July. The recapture of the city made a memorial of the well, and a method of the reprisal.
story: Colonial memory froze this day. Indian dead in the taking of Kanpur and in the Doab did not get a well with a grate.

sides.label: Nana Sahib’s forces / local actors at the Bibighar

casualties.sideLabel: British women and children at the Bibighar
casualties.note: Contemporary British lists name most of the Bibighar dead; totals vary with who is counted at the ghat as well.

reports.outlet: Andrew Ward, Our Bones Are Scattered
reports.headline: A well, and a reprisal
reports.excerpt: Kanpur is two files: the killing of prisoners, and the killing that followed when the city was taken back. Histories that keep only one file are doing a job.

reports.headline: Cawnpore and the well
reports.excerpt: The Bibighar killings of 15 July 1857 froze colonial memory. Indian dead in the taking of Kanpur did not get a well with a grate.

name: Delhi recaptured
summary: The Company army came down from the Ridge on 14 September. Street fighting lasted days. The city was sacked. Bahadur Shah was taken at Humayun’s tomb. Indian dead in the recapture were never given a number that both sides accepted.

casualties.note: No agreed integer. Contemporary British officers describe wholesale killing; later Indian and academic accounts treat the recapture as a sack.

reports.headline: A city made an example
reports.excerpt: The Ridge to the Fort is a military narrative. The lanes between them are a massacre the files never quite totalled.

reports.headline: The recapture of Delhi
reports.excerpt: The Company came down from the Ridge on 14 September. Street fighting lasted days. The city was sacked. No agreed integer for the Indian dead.

name: Siege of the Lucknow Residency
summary: The Residency was held from July until relief in November, then the city was abandoned and retaken in 1858. Awadh’s taluqdars and peasants made the siege possible; the Company’s guns ended it.

casualties.note: Garrison casualties are in British returns; city deaths across the two takings of Lucknow are not a single figure.

reports.headline: A residency, a province
reports.excerpt: Lucknow is a siege in British memory and a peasant war in Awadh’s.

reports.headline: The siege of Lucknow
reports.excerpt: The Residency is a siege in British memory and a peasant war in Awadh’s. Garrison casualties are in the returns; the city’s are not.

name: Jhansi
summary: Hugh Rose took Jhansi in April 1858. Lakshmibai escaped and died at Gwalior in June. The lapse of her adopted son’s state had been paperwork; the storm of the fort was not.

casualties.note: Storms of forts in 1858 produced high Indian deaths that were not census-counted.

reports.outlet: Tapti Roy, The Politics of a Popular Uprising
reports.headline: A rani, a lapse, a fort
reports.excerpt: Jhansi enters the nationalist canon as a woman on a horse. The files are a siege and a doctrine.

reports.headline: Jhansi, 1858
reports.excerpt: Hugh Rose took the fort in April. Lakshmibai escaped and died at Gwalior. The lapse of her adopted son’s state had been paperwork.

name: Tirurangadi
summary: A clash at Tirurangadi in August 1921 is the conventional start of the Malabar rebellion. Khilafat volunteers, tenancy, and a police raid met. Eranad went to war.

sides.label: Malabar police and British Indian troops

reports.outlet: R. H. Hitchcock, A History of the Malabar Rebellion
reports.headline: Eranad goes out
reports.excerpt: The official history begins at a police station. The tenancy file had been open for years.

reports.headline: The Moplah rebellion in the Commons
reports.excerpt: Parliament’s Malabar file begins at a police station in August 1921. The tenancy file had been open for years.

name: Wagon Tragedy
summary: About a hundred Mappila prisoners were shut in a goods wagon at Tirur for the journey to Podanur. By the time the doors were opened, most of them had suffocated. The official count of the dead is 64 to 70.

casualties.note: The suffocation deaths are unusually well documented for a colonial repression file. 70 is the figure commonly used; some returns give 64.

reports.outlet: Inquiry into the Tirur wagon deaths
reports.headline: A closed wagon on the Malabar line
reports.excerpt: Seventy men can die of air in a moving jail. The rebellion had already become a file of methods.

reports.headline: The wagon tragedy of 1921
reports.excerpt: About a hundred Mappila prisoners were shut in a goods wagon at Tirur. By Podanur most of them had suffocated. The official dead: 64 to 70.

reports.headline: The Moplah train disaster
reports.excerpt: The Commons was told of men dead of air in a moving jail. The rebellion had already become a file of methods.

name: Birsa captured
summary: Birsa Munda was taken in early February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June. The ulgulan outlived him as a name.

reports.outlet: K. S. Singh, Birsa Munda and His Movement
reports.headline: A prophet in a jail
reports.excerpt: The capture is a police date. The tenancy act is the longer sentence.

reports.headline: Birsa Munda, the Ulgulan, and a jail in Ranchi
reports.excerpt: Arrested on 3 February 1900 in the forests of Porahat. Died in Ranchi jail on 9 June. Colonial records said cholera. The tenancy act is the longer sentence.

name: Alluri Sitarama Raju killed
summary: Raju was shot on 7 May 1924 after two years in the Manyam. Police accounts call it an encounter. His name stayed in the hills.

sides.label: Madras Police / Malabar Special Police detachments

reports.outlet: Agency police reports / later Andhra histories
reports.headline: A rifle in the Manyam
reports.excerpt: The forest law stayed. The man who raided stations for rifles did not.

reports.headline: A rifle in the Manyam
reports.excerpt: Between August 1922 and May 1924 Alluri led the Rampa rising against forest law. He was captured, tied to a tree, and shot on 7 May 1924.

name: Ryots refuse indigo, Nadia
summary: In March 1859 ryots in Nadia refused the indigo contract. The Biswas brothers of the Krishnanagar countryside led the first combination. Planters used the lathiyal; peasants used the field. An official commission followed.

reports.headline: Indigo Revolt
reports.excerpt: The revolt began as a strike in a Nadia village in March 1859 and spread through the indigo districts. Nil Darpan put the coercion on a Calcutta stage the next year.

reports.headline: The forgotten revolution of the 1850s
reports.excerpt: The dam broke in Krishnagar, Nadia, where the Biswas brothers led peasants against the planters. The crop’s coercion was never quite the same.

name: Pabna agrarian league
summary: Tenants in Yusufshahi pargana formed a league against zamindari rent hikes in May 1873. The method was combination and the court more than the pike. The Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885 is part of its after.

reports.headline: Pabna Peasant Uprising
reports.excerpt: The Pabna Raiyats’ League came into existence in May 1873. Lieutenant-Governor Campbell told zamindars to assert claims by law only. The movement subsided into a legal file, then a tenancy act.

name: Supa, Deccan riots
summary: On 12 May 1875, market day at Supa, cultivators attacked Gujarati and Marwari moneylenders’ houses and burned the bond-chests. The riots spread through Poona and Ahmednagar. A commission followed; the Deccan Agriculturists’ Relief Act of 1879 is the legal after.

reports.headline: How the Deccan riots of 1875 laid a paper trail
reports.excerpt: The rioters’ purpose was the bonds, decrees and deeds. A commission sat. The Relief Act of 1879 is the longer sentence.

reports.headline: Agrarian unrest: the Deccan riots of 1875
reports.excerpt: The Deccan Riots Commission found the combustible elements everywhere ready. Physical crime was small beside the burning of paper.

name: Gandhi at Motihari court
summary: Gandhi reached Motihari on 15 April 1917 for the indigo ryots still held to tinkathia. On 18 April he told the magistrate he would not leave the district. The case was withdrawn. A provincial Act followed.

reports.headline: Champaran: India’s first satyagraha
reports.excerpt: The evening he reached Motihari he was ordered out. He appeared in court, pleaded guilty to remaining, and stayed. A local grievance became a national method.

reports.headline: When Gandhi arrived in Bihar
reports.excerpt: Thousands assembled before Motihari court on 18 April 1917. The tinkathia system was the file. Satyagraha was the method.
